successCriteria.description: The shared types module exports a LeaveType enum whose members map to exactly the six string values 'annual', 'sick', 'emergency', 'unpaid', 'maternity', 'paternity' — no more, no fewer.
The shared types module exports a LeaveRequestStatus enum whose members map to exactly the five string values 'DRAFT', 'SUBMITTED', 'APPROVED', 'REJECTED', 'CANCELLED' — no more, no fewer.
The shared types module exports a UserRole enum whose members map to exactly the three string values 'employee', 'manager', 'hr_admin' — no more, no fewer.

The base repository exposes six query-helper operations (query, findById, findAll, insert, update, delete) that execute SQL against the pg pool and return the documented result shapes: findById returns the row or null when absent; findAll returns an array (empty when none); insert returns the inserted row; update returns the updated row or null when no match; delete returns a boolean indicating whether a row was removed.

The base repository is an abstract class that cannot be instantiated directly and is designed to be extended by concrete repositories; all six methods route database access through the shared pool, satisfying the repository-pattern rule (no direct DB access outside the repository layer).

The base repository uses TypeScript generics throughout and contains no `any` types — params are typed as `unknown[]`, row data as `Record<string, unknown>`, and caught errors as `unknown`; the project compiles cleanly under strict TypeScript (tsc --noEmit).
Jest unit tests cover each base repository method across success, not-found/null, empty, and error-propagation paths, and the full test suite passes (npx jest --passWithNoTests exits 0).

constraints: No `any` types anywhere in the shared types or base repository — use `unknown` with type guards and TypeScript generics instead (HARNESS.json constraint `no-any`, severity high; enforced by tsconfig strict mode).

All database access must go through the repository layer — the base repository encapsulates the pg pool; no inline SQL or direct pool usage may occur outside repository classes (HARNESS.json constraint `no-direct-db-outside-repository`, severity critical; GP-001).
The base repository must import and use the `pool` exported from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` rather than constructing its own Pool instance.

The three enums must be string-valued enums whose member values exactly match the reconciled architecture's specified string literals (LeaveType: annual|sick|emergency|unpaid|maternity|paternity; LeaveRequestStatus: DRAFT|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|REJECTED|CANCELLED; UserRole: employee|manager|hr_admin).
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens in the shared types or base repository (HARNESS.json constraint `no-hardcoded-secrets`, severity critical).
No unhandled promise rejections — all async errors in the base repository must be caught and re-thrown in a typed manner (GP-006); the catch blocks must type the error as `unknown`.
outOfScope: The optional `client: PoolClient` transaction parameter is NOT part of this phase's base repository helpers — transactional client support is deferred to the concrete Pg*Repository classes in Phases 2–7 per the Transaction Contract.

Concrete domain repositories (Employee, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest, AuditLog, Notification) and their entity models are out of scope — they are built in Phases 2–7 and will extend the base repository.
Service layers, controllers, Fastify routes, RBAC guards, and audit/notification wiring are out of scope — they belong to Phases 8–10.
Database migrations / schema creation (Knex) for the conceptual tables are out of scope for this phase — the base repository operates against tables assumed to exist.

SQL injection hardening of the dynamic table-name/column-name interpolation in the base repository's generic helpers is a known limitation of the generic pattern; concrete repositories in later phases own parameterized, validated queries for their specific tables. This phase does not add a sanitization layer.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum is a closed set of exactly six string values; no leave category outside annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity is representable, and every LeavePolicy in later phases must reference one of these values.

The enum is a closed set of exactly five string values that govern the LeaveRequest lifecycle; the valid transitions (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED|REJECTED|CANCELLED; APPROVED→CANCELLED; DRAFT→CANCELLED) are defined by the reconciled architecture and enforced by later-phase services, but the enum itself must expose all five states.

The enum is a closed set of exactly three string values (employee, manager, hr_admin) that drive RBAC across the entire system; the auth contract binds request.user.role to one of these values, and no other role may be introduced in this phase.

BaseRepository is an abstract class that cannot be instantiated directly; it provides generic query helpers that all concrete Pg*Repository classes extend, ensuring every database access path flows through the repository layer (GP-001).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Errors from the underlying pg pool must propagate to the caller as re-thrown exceptions (caught as `unknown`, re-thrown); no silent swallowing.
Returns the matching row or null when no row exists; pool errors propagate as re-thrown exceptions.
Returns an array of all rows (empty array when the table has none); pool errors propagate as re-thrown exceptions.
Returns the inserted row (via RETURNING *); constraint-violation and other pool errors propagate as re-thrown exceptions.
Returns the updated row or null when no row matches the id (via RETURNING *); pool errors propagate as re-thrown exceptions.
Returns true when a row was removed, false when no row matched; pool errors propagate as re-thrown exceptions.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The base repository must import and use the `pool` symbol exactly as exported from the database connection module — no alternate Pool construction or connection-string handling.

The three enums' string values must match the reconciled architecture's declared enum values exactly (LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, UserRole) so that every downstream module (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit, notification) can import them as the single source of truth.
The shared-types module boundary (src/shared/types/) and its ownership of the three enums must match the reconciled module-boundaries table; no other module may redefine these enums.

The base repository must satisfy the repository-pattern rule and the no-direct-db-outside-repository constraint as stated in the golden principles and HARNESS.json — all pool access is encapsulated inside the repository abstraction.
The UserRole enum values must match the auth contract's declared role set (employee | manager | hr_admin) so that request.user.role typing and RBAC guards in later phases are consistent.

integrationPoints.why: The base repository depends on the shared pool for all query execution; this is the single integration surface between the repository layer and PostgreSQL.

integrationPoints.target: Concrete Pg*Repository classes (Phases 2–7: Employee, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest, AuditLog, Notification)
integrationPoints.why: All concrete repositories extend BaseRepository and inherit the six generic query helpers; the base class is the foundation they build upon.

integrationPoints.target: All domain modules (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit, notification)
integrationPoints.why: Every domain module imports the three enums from src/shared/types/index.ts as the single source of truth for LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, and UserRole — the dependency map shows shared-types as the root dependency of all modules.
The UserRole enum is consumed by the auth contract (request.user.role) and the requireRole RBAC guard; its values must be stable for the guard wiring in the final phase.
